Q: Declaring a variable as 'local' when outside Lua functions A:

Even tough I can't say I know Lua, from use of the language, I believe people are describing this the wrong way. In my understanding, a local declaration outside functions is just a declaration that executes whenever the file's code is run. Whenever the file is run, it only takes precedence over global declarations with same name. It is not local to the file, in any sense.

It is not local to the file, because if you require the file, any value assigned to the "local" variable outside any function will override the value of a same-named local variable at the file where the require is executed. As a result, the following code makes keyword "local" counterintuitive.

-- foo.lua

local a = 5
local b = 0

return b

-- main.lua

local a = 3

local b = require('foo')

print("a="..a)

because this prints "a=5"!

So, I don't know what is the proper terminology that can disambiguate these things, but Lua (and any language) should be making better choices, in my opinion. E.g., keyword "local" could have been "override", which would explain the semantics I have come across at least.

Maybe, a way to describe the semantics is that there is a global scope (inside or outside functions, w/o any scope keyword), a global-local scope (outside functions using keyword "local") that overrides the global scope and a local scope (inside functions, using "local" keyword) that overrides both global and global-local scopes. Variables with same name, in one of those scopes, are the same variable.

Q: KQL Script to check existence of a file on Azure VM file system A:

Can you elaborate more? I would guess by KQL you mean Kusto Query Language which is not script language but query language. KQL is used in Azure Resource Graph but Azure resource graph provides inventory information only for Azure resources. Azure VMs are Azure resources but any information inside the VMs is not something that is available in ARG, it is only for data of the VM in relationship of how it is defined in ARM when deployed. You could potentially use Azure Change Tracking and Inventory but I am not sure if it fully needs your needs due to no specific details provided and it might be overkill as the services is more for tracking changes rather just finding if specific file exists or not.
